result:
I evaluated http://127.0.0.1:3100/fluxo.html and found 7 defects. The report was sent to `POST /api/submit` and the server accepted it (HTTP 200, status "aceito", file `2026-09-18T09-15-22-com-run1-0c06e43e.json`).

- `.link-opcao` — `govbr-3.7.0-accessibility-global-21fbcc2fe37b`: the 4 links under "Outras opções" show no focus indicator. A CSS rule sets both outline and box-shadow to none.
- `.mensagem-erro-cpf` — `govbr-3.7.0-accessibility-global-cc837bbaf713`: the error message is not linked to `#cpf` (no `aria-describedby`).
- `.mensagem-erro-cpf` — `wcag:4.1.3`: the error message is not announced to screen readers. It has no `role=alert` or `aria-live`, and focus moves to `<body>`.
- `.mensagem-erro-cpf` — `ds-token-color`: the text colour `#e60000` is not a DS token. `verify_finding` confirmed this against the live page (V-001).
- `.lista-opcoes` — `ds-token-color`: the border colour `#dee2e6` is not a DS token.
- `.opcao-identificacao` — `ds-token-spacing`: the 4 option items use `padding: 13px`, which is off the DS spacing scale.
- `#cpf` — `ds-structure-input-tag`: the `br-input` class is on the `<input>` itself as well as on its wrapper `<div>`.

The three `.mensagem-erro-cpf` findings only exist after clicking "Continuar" with the CPF field empty.

**What I tested:** I checked the accessibility tree and moved focus through every link, button and the input. I submitted the form empty and with "123", and ran the validator scan in the initial and error states. The automated accessibility check (axe) found no violations in either state.

**Left out and noted as limitations in the report:**
- "123" is accepted with no validation message and no navigation.
- The input has no `aria-invalid` in the error state.
- The option links have no underline.
- I didn't check what the Alto Contraste and VLibras buttons actually do.
- I didn't test narrow screen widths.
- The validator's notes without a backing rule (extra classes, the 11px tag text, `<hr role=presentation>`) are not reported as findings.
